title: React GraphQL Applied Check
description: Apply GraphQL and Apollo Client knowledge to variables, mutation results, optimistic UI, normalized cache identity, pagination pitfalls, subscriptions, auth headers, and error handling.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A query hardcodes `user(id: "1")` in the document and the component needs different users. What is better?

options.text: Use GraphQL variables, such as `query User($id: ID!) { user(id: $id) { id name } }`
Build the query string with unsafe concatenation every render
Use a CSS class for the id
Fetch all users and ignore the id

questions.explanation: Variables keep operations reusable and avoid manual query string construction.

questions.prompt: A mutation creates a todo but returns only `{ success }`. The UI needs the new todo in the list. What is the likely problem?

options.text: The mutation response does not include enough fields for the cache or UI to add the item
GraphQL mutations cannot return objects
Apollo cannot run mutations from React
The query must be renamed to CSS

questions.explanation: Mutation payloads should often return the changed entity fields, including id and typename, so UI and cache updates have the data they need.

questions.prompt: Which optimistic mutation practices are important? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Provide enough temporary object identity for the optimistic cache entry
Plan for rollback or correction when the server rejects the mutation
Keep the optimistic response shape compatible with the mutation selection
Assume optimistic updates can never fail

questions.explanation: Optimistic responses must match the selected shape and need a failure path when the server result differs or errors.

questions.prompt: Two different `Comment` objects have no `id` in query results. What cache issue can appear?

options.text: Apollo may not be able to normalize and update those objects reliably by identity
GraphQL will refuse to return arrays
React will stop rendering strings
Subscriptions become impossible in all cases

questions.explanation: Stable identifiers such as id plus __typename are central to normalized cache identity.

questions.prompt: A paginated feed query uses the same cache field for every cursor without a type policy. What can go wrong?

options.text: Pages may overwrite or merge incorrectly because the cache does not know the pagination strategy
The server will delete old posts automatically
GraphQL variables stop working
The component becomes a Server Component

questions.explanation: Pagination often needs field policies or explicit merge logic so pages combine correctly without corrupting order or duplicates.

questions.prompt: A subscription event that updates an entity should still respect the normalized cache shape and object identity.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Subscription payloads should include enough fields for Apollo to update or write entities consistently.

questions.prompt: A GraphQL API returns partial data with an `errors` array. What should the UI consider?

options.text: GraphQL can return data and errors together, so the UI may need to handle partial success explicitly
Errors always mean there is no data field
React will throw automatically for every GraphQL error
The response is invalid JSON

questions.explanation: GraphQL responses can include both partial data and errors. Apollo configuration and UI logic should account for that possibility.

questions.prompt: Where should an Apollo auth token commonly be attached for HTTP operations?

options.text: In a link or request middleware that sets an Authorization header when a token exists
In every GraphQL field name
In a CSS custom property
Only inside the component title

questions.explanation: Apollo links are a common place to centralize headers such as Authorization without repeating them in every component.
